messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-20318 — High 5xx rate from inference-prod-east (route: /v1/generate). Current error rate: 18% over 2m, latency spike to 850ms. Escalation policy: primary -> secondary -> manager. Link: https://pd.example.com/incidents/PD-20318

pagerduty-bot: Notification sent to primary on-call: @sam. If unacknowledged within 3m, will escalate to secondary.

sam (oncall): saw mobile ping, on a train with flaky signal. trying to ack but pager not connecting. @jia can you take if i can't ack?

(2m later) pagerduty-bot: Alert not acknowledged by primary. Auto-escalating to secondary: @jia. Manager will be notified on missed ack.

jia (secondary): acked the incident — I'm on it. quick triage: error traces point to model shard nodes 7-9 throwing OOM / grpc EOFs. Traffic spike looks normal, something's causing memory growth on those hosts.

jia (secondary): immediate mitigation plan: 1) remove shard nodes 7-9 from load balancer; 2) scale inference-runtime deployment by +3 replicas in that AZ; 3) enable fallback model variant (quantized) for latency-sensitive routes. I'll start step 1 now.

ops-bot: Running command to drain nodes 7-9: `./infra/drain-node.sh shard-7 && ./infra/drain-node.sh shard-8 && ./infra/drain-node.sh shard-9`

jia (secondary): drain started, doing healthchecks. hooking up proxy to route new requests away from those shards.

carla (manager): got the escalation. update me when we know customer impact (top 10 impacted orgs) and ETA to restore.

jia (secondary): current customer impact: 12 orgs seeing >=10% error increase; some high-volume customers report request timeouts in the last 5m. Gathering request IDs for support.

sam (oncall): finally acked — lost signal earlier, sorry. I'm moving to laptop now, happy to assist with runbook steps or do a handoff.

jia (secondary): handoff not required, but pls monitor logs for regressions. I'm scaling now: `kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-runtime --replicas=24` — scaling command issued.

ops-bot: Scaling acknowledged. New pods initializing (5 additional). Healthchecks 0/5 -> 5/5 across AZ after 45s.

jia (secondary): enabling model fallback for /v1/generate on the edge routing rule for production-weighted traffic: set `model_variant=fallback-quant-8bit` for route tag `latency-sensitive`. Pushing config.

sre-runbooks: Reminder: if enabling fallback, monitor quality regressions — make sure to tag evals. Also note token cost will change for customers using embeddings.

jia (secondary): fallback in effect for 40% of traffic. Error rate dropped to 4% within 1m, latency back to ~220ms for fallback requests. Still seeing some 503s from residual shard connections.

carla (manager): good. can you estimate full recovery ETA? Also prepare a short customer note: what happened and what we did.

jia (secondary): estimate: 10-15m to finish draining bad shards and fully shift traffic. customer note draft: "We observed increased 5xx errors due to memory pressure on inference shard hosts. We drained affected nodes, scaled runtime, and enabled a fallback quantized model to restore service while we fix the underlying host instability."

sam (oncall): looking at node metrics now — saw a memory leak pattern starting ~03:05 UTC from an autoscaler misconfig change in an earlier canary deploy. file /var/log/runtime/oom.log shows repeated allocations. creating issue: INFRA-4567.

jia (secondary): nice catch. can you put that in the incident timeline? I'll mark mitigation steps as completed once draining finishes.

ops-bot: Drain complete for shard-7/8/9. Nodes removed from lb and cordoned.

jia (secondary): confirmed. error rate down to 1.2% and latency normalized to 120-180ms. rerouting remaining traffic back to new pods.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-20318 acknowledged by @jia at 1726789150. Auto-notifications to manager @carla fired at 1726789180 (missed primary ack).

carla (manager): thanks team. please attach a CI ticket and postmortem link when available. do we need a customer-facing status page update?

sam (oncall): I'll open postmortem. short-term: revert the autoscaler change from canary and roll a patched runtime with guardrails.

jia (secondary): marking mitigation complete and moving to monitoring. PD incident status: under control.

incident-bot: PD-20318 status updated: Resolved (mitigation applied). Time to mitigation: ~6m. Root cause: memory leak triggered by bad autoscaler config in canary deploy (investigating).

carla (manager): good job. next steps: sam to file postmortem (assign INFRA-4567), engineering to patch the runtime and add limiters in autoscaler config, SRE to run a follow-up on similar canaries.

sam (oncall): will file postmortem now and ping stakeholders.

jia (secondary): closing the slack thread — will stay watch for 30m. if anything flares I'll reopen PD. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-20318 closed at 1726789612.

carla (manager): note for postmortem: missed primary ack window — consider extending primary ack window to 5m for on-call travel or set up a primary fallback plan.

sre-runbooks: adding action item: update runbook step 2 to include immediate fallback model toggle and explicit LB-drain command snippet.

sam (oncall): again, apologies for unavailability earlier. learning: always have a secondary pre-briefed.

jia (secondary): no worries. great teamwork. we kept customer impact limited."
